questions.question: Simplify: (4.5 − 2 \(\frac{1}{4}\) ) + ( \(3\frac35\) ÷ 0.6)
questions.questionHtml: Simplify: (4.5 − 2\(\frac{1}{4}\)) + (\(3\frac35\) ÷ 0.6)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick
⇒ (4.5 - 9/4) + \(\frac{18}{5} \div \frac{6}{10}\)

⇒ (4.5 - 2.25) + \(\frac{18}{5} \times \frac{10}{6}\)

⇒ 2.25 + (3 × 2)

⇒ 2.25 + 6

⇒ 8.25

questions.question: Rahul invested 1,20,000 in a business. After 4 months, Suresh joined with 90,000. After another 4 months, Rahul withdrew 40,000. Find their profit sharing ratio after 1 year.
questions.questionHtml: Rahul invested 1,20,000 in a business. After 4 months, Suresh joined with 90,000. After another 4 months, Rahul withdrew 40,000. Find their profit sharing ratio after 1 year.
questions.solution:
Rahul's money for first 8 months: 120000 × 8 ⇒ 960000.

Rahul withdraws 40000: New investment = 80000; last 4 months: 80000 × 4 ⇒ 320000.

Total Rahul investment value: 960000 + 320000 ⇒ 1280000.

Suresh invests after 4 months: duration = 8 months; Suresh investment value = 90000 × 8 ⇒ 720000.

Ratio Rahul : Suresh = 1280000 : 720000 ⇒ 16 : 9.

questions.question: A test has 150 questions divided into three sections: Section A (30 questions), Section B (60 questions), and Section C (60 questions). A candidate answers 60% of Section A, 50% of Section B, and 40% of Section C correctly. If the minimum passing score is 60%, how many more questions must the candidate answer correctly to pass?
questions.questionHtml: A test has 150 questions divided into three sections: Section A (30 questions), Section B (60 questions), and Section C (60 questions). A candidate answers 60% of Section A, 50% of Section B, and 40% of Section C correctly. If the minimum passing score is 60%, how many more questions must the candidate answer correctly to pass?
questions.solution:
⇒ Correct in Section A = 60% × 30 = 18

⇒ Correct in Section B = 50% × 60 = 30

⇒ Correct in Section C = 40% × 60 = 24

⇒ Total correct answers = 18 + 30 + 24 = 72

⇒ Passing marks = 60% × 150 = 90

⇒ More questions needed = 90 − 72 = 18

questions.question: A shopkeeper buys pens at 6 for ₹30, 5 for ₹28, and 4 for ₹24. He mixes them in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5 and sells the mixture at 5 for ₹34. Find his approximate gain or loss percentage.
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper buys pens at 6 for ₹30, 5 for ₹28, and 4 for ₹24. He mixes them in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5 and sells the mixture at 5 for ₹34. Find his approximate gain or loss percentage.
questions.solution:
⇒ Total pens = 2 + 3 + 5 = 10

⇒ Total cost = (2 × 5) + (3 × 5.6) + (5 × 6) = ₹56.8

⇒ Cost price per pen = 56.8 ÷ 10 = ₹5.68

⇒ Selling price per pen = ₹6.8

⇒ Gain per pen = 6.8 − 5.68 = ₹1.12

⇒ Gain % = (1.12 ÷ 5.68) × 100 ≈ 19.7%

∴ Approximate gain = 20%

questions.question: A trader sells three types of bags such that the ratio of their selling prices is 2 : 3 : 5. He makes a gain of 20% on the first, 10% on the second, and a loss of 10% on the third. Find his approximate overall gain or loss percentage.
questions.questionHtml: A trader sells three types of bags such that the ratio of their selling prices is 2 : 3 : 5. He makes a gain of 20% on the first, 10% on the second, and a loss of 10% on the third. Find his approximate overall gain or loss percentage.
questions.solution:
Let selling prices be 2x, 3x, 5x.

CP of first = 2x ÷ 1.2 = 1.667x, CP of second = 3x ÷ 1.1 = 2.727x, CP of third = 5x ÷ 0.9 = 5.556x.

Total SP = 2x + 3x + 5x = 10x, Total CP = 1.667x + 2.727x + 5.556x = 9.95x.

Gain = 10x − 9.95x = 0.05x, Gain % = (0.05x ÷ 9.95x) × 100 ≈ 0.5%.

questions.question: A and B can do a job in 10 and 15 days respectively. They work together for 3 days and then B leaves. How many more days will A take to finish the work?
questions.questionHtml: A and B can do a job in 10 and 15 days respectively. They work together for 3 days and then B leaves. How many more days will A take to finish the work?
questions.solution:
⇒ LCM of 10 and 15 = 30 units (Total work)

⇒ A's 1 day work = 30 ÷ 10 = 3 units/day, B's 1 day work = 30 ÷ 15 = 2 units/day

⇒ Work done in 3 days = (3 + 2) × 3 = 15 units

⇒ Remaining work = 30 − 15 = 15 units

⇒ Required days = 15 ÷ 3 = 5 days

questions.question: Two qualities of rice costing 60 per kg and another quality are mixed in the ratio 5:3. The mixture is sold at 54 per kg with no profit or loss. Find the cost of the second quality.
questions.questionHtml: Two qualities of rice costing 60 per kg and another quality are mixed in the ratio 5:3. The mixture is sold at 54 per kg with no profit or loss. Find the cost of the second quality.
questions.solution:
Total quantity = 5 + 3 = 8 kg

Total cost = (5 × 60) + (3 × x)

(300 + 3x) ÷ 8 = 54 ⇒ 300 + 3x = 432 ⇒ 3x = 132 ⇒ x = 44

∴ The cost of the second quality of rice is ₹44 per kg.

questions.question: A and B together can complete a work in 24 days. After working together for 8 days, B alone finishes the remaining work in 32 days. In how many days can B alone do the entire work?
questions.questionHtml: A and B together can complete a work in 24 days. After working together for 8 days, B alone finishes the remaining work in 32 days. In how many days can B alone do the entire work?
questions.solution:
Total work = 24 units (LCM of time values).

Work completed in 8 days by (A + B) = 8 × 1 = 8 units; Remaining work = 24 − 8 = 16 units.

B's 1 day work = 16 ÷ 32 = 0.5 units/day; Time taken by B alone = 24 ÷ 0.5 = 48 days.

questions.question: A vessel contains milk, water and juice in the ratio 4 : 5 : 3. 24 litres of mixture is removed and replaced by 10 litres of milk and 6 litres of juice. If water becomes 12 litres more than milk, find the initial quantity.
questions.questionHtml: A vessel contains milk, water and juice in the ratio 4 : 5 : 3. 24 litres of mixture is removed and replaced by 10 litres of milk and 6 litres of juice. If water becomes 12 litres more than milk, find the initial quantity.
questions.solution:
Let initial total quantity = 12x litres ⇒ Milk = 4x, Water = 5x, Juice = 3x.

Fraction removed = 24 ÷ 12x = 2 ÷ x.

Milk removed = 4x × 2 ÷ x = 8, Water removed = 5x × 2 ÷ x = 10, Juice removed = 3x × 2 ÷ x = 6.

Milk left = 4x − 8 + 10 = 4x + 2, Water left = 5x − 10, Juice left = 3x.

Given: Water = Milk + 12 ⇒ 5x − 10 = (4x + 2) + 12 ⇒ 5x − 10 = 4x + 14 ⇒ x = 24.

Initial quantity = 12x = 12 × 24 = 288 litres.

questions.question: A car covers a distance at 72 km per hour in 2 hours. If it takes 30 minutes more due to traffic, by what fraction should the speed be reduced?
questions.questionHtml: A car covers a distance at 72 km per hour in 2 hours. If it takes 30 minutes more due to traffic, by what fraction should the speed be reduced?
questions.solution:
⇒ Distance = 72 × 2 = 144 km

⇒ New time = 2 + 0.5 = 2.5 hours

⇒ New speed = 144 ÷ 2.5 = 57.6 km/h

⇒ Fraction reduced = (72 − 57.6) ÷ 72 = 14.4 ÷ 72 = 1 ÷ 5

∴ The correct answer is 1/5.

questions.question: The cost of fencing a circular park at 110 per metre is 3,454. Find the radius of the park.
questions.questionHtml: The cost of fencing a circular park at 110 per metre is 3,454. Find the radius of the park.
questions.solution:
Fencing cost per metre = 110, Total fencing cost = 3454.

⇒ Perimeter = 3454 ÷ 110 = 31.4 m

⇒ 2πr = 31.4, using π = 3.14.

⇒ 2 × 3.14 × r = 31.4 ⇒ r = 31.4 ÷ 6.28 = 5 m.

questions.question: A circle of radius 10 cm is inscribed in a square. Find the area of the unused part of the square.
questions.questionHtml: A circle of radius 10 cm is inscribed in a square. Find the area of the unused part of the square.
questions.solution:
Area of square = 20 × 20 = 400 cm2

Area of circle = π × 10 × 10 = 100π cm2

Unused area = 400 − 100π = 400 − 314 = 86 cm2

questions.question: A circular wheel makes 60 revolution per minutes and has a radius of 21 cm. Find the distance travelled by a wheel in 20 minutes. Use π = 22/7.
questions.questionHtml: A circular wheel makes 60 revolution per minutes and has a radius of 21 cm. Find the distance travelled by a wheel in 20 minutes. Use π = 22/7.
questions.solution:
⇒ Circumference = 2 × π × r = 2 × 22 ÷ 7 × 21 = 132 cm

⇒ Total revolutions in 20 minutes = 60 × 20 = 1200

⇒ Distance travelled = 132 × 1200 = 158400 cm = 1584 m

questions.question: Find the slope of a line perpendicular to y = 4x − 5.
questions.questionHtml: Find the slope of a line perpendicular to y = 4x − 5.
questions.solution:
⇒ Slope of given line = 4

Let perpendicular slope = m

⇒ 4 × m = −1

⇒ m = −1 ÷ 4

∴ The correct answer is −1/4.

questions.question: Given x − 1/x = 4, find the value of x 2 + 1/x 2
questions.questionHtml: Given x − 1/x = 4, find the value of x<sup>2</sup> + 1/x<sup>2</sup>
questions.solution:
Given: x − 1 ÷ x = 4

(x − 1 ÷ x)2 = x2 + 1 ÷ x2 − 2

⇒ 42 = x2 + 1 ÷ x2 − 2

⇒ x2 + 1 ÷ x2 = 16 + 2 = 18

∴ The correct answer is 18.
